section: Romans 8:29 — Foreknowledge, Predestination, and the Divine Decrees: Steps One and Two of the Five Steps to Glory
text: Romans 8:29 — Foreknowledge, Predestination, and the Divine Decrees: Steps One and Two of the Five Steps to Glory

section: Romans 8:29 — Foreknowledge, Predestination, and the Divine Decrees: Steps One and Two of the Five Steps to Glory
text: Romans 8:29 “For those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, in order that he might be the firstborn among many brothers.” (ESV)

section: Romans 8:29 — Foreknowledge, Predestination, and the Divine Decrees: Steps One and Two of the Five Steps to Glory
text: Corrected translation: For whom He foreknew, He also fore-ordained — conformed ones to the image of His Son.

section: Romans 8:29 — Foreknowledge, Predestination, and the Divine Decrees: Steps One and Two of the Five Steps to Glory
text: Romans 8:28 established that all things work together for the purpose of God for those who are the called ones according to the predetermined plan. Verses 29 and 30 now provide the mechanical explanation of how all things work together for good, presenting what may be called the five steps to glory. Steps one and two are found in verse 29. This chapter examines both steps in detail, together with the doctrinal framework of omniscience, the divine decrees, and foreknowledge that underlies them.

section: I. The Connecting Conjunction and the Verb of Cognizance
text: I. The Connecting Conjunction and the Verb of Cognizance

section: I. The Connecting Conjunction and the Verb of Cognizance
text: Verse 29 opens with a conjunction that connects this verse directly to Romans 8:28. The conjunction is used after verbs of cognizance to express the content of that cognizance — it signals that what follows is the known doctrinal content of what was affirmed in the preceding verse. The conjunction therefore demands the repetition of the first-person plural perfect indicative verb from verse 28.

section: I. The Connecting Conjunction and the Verb of Cognizance
text: The verb repeated from verse 28 is oidamen (οἴδαμεν), the perfect active indicative of oida (οἶδα). The perfect functions as a present of existing state: we know. The conjunction following it is hoti (ὅτι), introducing the content of that knowledge. Corrected translation of the opening: We know that.

section: II. Step One — Reality in the Mind of God: Foreknowledge (Romans 8:29a)
text: II. Step One — Reality in the Mind of God: Foreknowledge (Romans 8:29a)

section: A. The Relative Pronoun and Its Force
text: A. The Relative Pronoun and Its Force

section: A. The Relative Pronoun and Its Force
text: Following oidamen hoti comes the accusative masculine singular of the relative pronoun hos (ὅς), functioning as a direct object: whom. This pronoun establishes the object of the divine action that follows — the class of persons who are the beneficiaries of the mechanics of the divine plan.

section: B. Proginōskō — The Verb of Divine Foreknowledge
text: B. Proginōskō — The Verb of Divine Foreknowledge

section: B. Proginōskō — The Verb of Divine Foreknowledge
text: The verb is the aorist active indicative of proginōskō (προγινώσκω). The compound is formed from pro (before) + ginōskō (γινώσκω, to know), yielding: to know beforehand, to know in advance, to have foreknowledge of something. In the New Testament this verb is used exclusively with God as its subject.

section: B. Proginōskō — The Verb of Divine Foreknowledge
text: The aorist is a constative aorist, gathering into one entirety the foreknowledge of God. The active voice indicates that the subject, God the Father as author of the divine plan, produces the action. The indicative mood is the declarative indicative, asserting the reality of the function of divine foreknowledge. Corrected translation to this point: We know that whom He foreknew.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Step one in the five steps to glory is that reality is in the mind of God — foreknowledge. To understand foreknowledge correctly, it must be distinguished from omniscience, with which it is frequently confused. The two terms refer to distinct operations of the divine intellect, and their relationship to the divine decrees is the key to the distinction.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: The relevant doctrinal points are as follows. The order is: omniscience → decrees → foreknowledge. This chronological sequence, though not the emphasis of Romans 8:29, is established elsewhere in Scripture, notably in Acts 2:23.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 1. Foreknowledge is more limited in its scope than the omniscience of God. Omniscience knows both the realities and all alternatives to those realities. Foreknowledge deals only with the realities — what actually occurs. Omniscience therefore precedes the decrees; foreknowledge follows the decrees.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 2. In omniscience, God knows perfectly and eternally all that is knowable, whether actual or possible — both the reality and every alternative to that reality.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 3. In foreknowledge, God deals with the reality only. Foreknowledge is the specific, restricted operation of divine cognition that acknowledges only what is contained in the divine decrees.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 4. Foreknowledge therefore refers only to those things which are adopted within the plan of God — only the reality, not the alternatives.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 5. In omniscience, God knows all that would have been adopted and knows an infinite number of alternatives to what occurred. Foreknowledge refers only to what God did in fact adopt and decree.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 6. Chronologically there is an order, but that chronological order is not in view in Romans 8:29. Romans 8:29 presents no chronological sequence; it presents instead the doctrinal reality that the foreknown, the predestined, and the elect are the same persons. The chronological order is in view in Acts 2:23.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 7. The important conclusion: election, foreknowledge, and predestination are coincidental with respect to their objects. There is no chronological sequence intended here. All three — foreknowledge, election, and predestination — are coincidental in respect to their objects, which in this age are the members of the royal family of God.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 8. Rather than a chronological order, Romans 8:29 expresses the doctrinal principle that the foreknown, the predestined, and the elect are the same persons. The believer is the beneficiary of all three simultaneously.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 9. Placing foreknowledge before the decrees chronologically would imply that another has caused what occurs, and that God is merely aware of what someone else has caused. That inference is blasphemous. The correct order is: omniscience, then the decrees, then foreknowledge.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 10. Omniscience knows both the reality and its alternatives. Only the reality is fed from omniscience into the decrees. Foreknowledge then acknowledges only what is in the decrees. Foreknowledge is not the totality of God's knowledge — it is that portion of divine cognition that corresponds to the decrees.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 11. The great principle: nothing can be foreknown until it is first decreed. Only the divine decrees establish reality.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 12. Only the divine decrees establish reality. All counterfactual or alternative history resides within omniscience alone.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 13. When it comes to chronology, omniscience and God's self-knowledge precede the decrees, while election and foreknowledge are actually the content of the decrees.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 14. Since the divine decrees establish certainty, nothing can be foreknown until it is first decreed. Hence the order: omniscience — then the decrees — then foreknowledge.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 15. Since foreknowledge deals only with what God decreed, it emphasizes that each believer was in the mind of God in eternity past. Every member of the royal family of God was personally known to God — by name, in detail — before time began.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 16. Divine thinking included every believer. No one is excluded from step one. God knows the full extent to which each believer will advance in the plan of God through the free exercise of volition. He knows which believers will reach maturity and which will not, which will die in dying grace and which will reach the sin unto death. All of these realities were in the decrees and therefore part of His foreknowledge.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 17. Divine thinking related to foreknowledge indicates that God has a plan for each believer's life.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step One: Foreknowledge Distinguished from Omniscience
text: Point 18. Everything was decreed simultaneously, not by stages. The mechanical breakdown of the five steps in this passage is designed to relate the believer to the plan of God, giving confidence and assurance, and setting forth a system of potentials and hopes as expressed in the X + Y + Z formula.

section: D. The Formula: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God
text: D. The Formula: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God

section: D. The Formula: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God
text: The five steps to glory, of which foreknowledge is step one, operate within the framework of seven divine imputations. The formula X + Y + Z = the glory of God (Romans 8:28) clarifies how foreknowledge and the decrees relate to the believer's advance through the plan of God.

section: D. The Formula: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God
text: X Radical: Human life imputed at birth + Adam's original sin imputed at birth = first potential (salvation). Plus the pertinent doctrine of the gospel = the first hope, confident assurance of salvation. The first plus: salvation adjustment to the justice of God through faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

section: D. The Formula: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God
text: Y Radical: Judicial imputation one — all personal sins imputed to Christ on the cross and judged. Judicial imputation two — the imputation of divine righteousness at salvation. These two together = the second potential (blessing in time). Plus pertinent doctrine = the second hope, confident assurance of maturity adjustment to the justice of God. The second plus: the reality of maturity adjustment replacing the hope.

section: D. The Formula: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God
text: Z Radical: Imputation of eternal life at salvation + the real imputation of blessing in time at the point of maturity = the third potential. Plus pertinent doctrine + undeserved suffering = the third hope. The third hope is the confident assurance of the seventh imputation — real imputation of eternal blessing and reward at the judgment seat of Christ. The equal sign: the glory of God.

section: D. The Formula: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God
text: God's foreknowledge extends across the full span of each believer's potential advance through this formula. A believer may stop at the first plus (salvation) and advance no further. God knew that billions of years ago. He also knew the alternatives — what would have been available had the believer continued. Omniscience contains those alternatives; the decrees and foreknowledge contain only the reality of how far each believer in fact advances.

section: III. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees
text: III. The Doctrine of Divine Decrees

section: A. Definition
text: A. Definition

section: A. Definition
text: The decrees of God are the sum total of God's plan designed in eternity past. They deal with reality only — what actually happens, not the alternatives. God's purposes relating to all events of every kind constitute one single, all-comprehensive intention, perceiving from omniscience all the events that occur in history, all the decisions, all the persons, conceiving the free as free and the necessary as necessary, together with all their causes, conditions, relations, and successions as one indivisible system of things, every link being related to the essential integrity of the whole.

section: B. The Will of God and the Decrees
text: B. The Will of God and the Decrees

section: B. The Will of God and the Decrees
text: The decrees represent the complete and consummated exercise of the will and sovereignty of God, determining the certain futurity of all events. No event is directly caused by the decrees. Rather, the decree itself provides in every case that events shall be affected by causes acting in a manner consistent with the nature of the event in question.

section: B. The Will of God and the Decrees
text: In the case of every free-will act of a moral agent, the decree provides five things simultaneously: (1) that the agent will be a free agent, acting without divine coercion; (2) that the antecedents of the act shall be what they are, without divine interference; (3) that all present conditions of the act shall be what they are; (4) that the act shall be perfectly spontaneous and free on the part of the agent; and (5) that the act shall be certainly future.

section: B. The Will of God and the Decrees
text: This means God does not stamp His will upon the believer's volition. The will of God represents what God desires for each believer — maximum blessing through the full advance from X through Y and Z to the seventh imputation. The decrees contain what each believer actually does. God can only decree reality. If a believer advances only to the first plus of the X radical, that is what was decreed — not because God willed it in the sense of desiring it, but because God's omniscience knew that the free will of that believer would take him no further. The will of God and the content of the decrees are therefore distinct.

section: B. The Will of God and the Decrees
text: The crucifixion of Christ illustrates this principle in its sharpest form (Acts 2:23). It was the sum total of human evil and reversionism, yet God's purpose was executed through the spontaneous free choices of those involved. Under the principle of efficacious grace, God the Holy Spirit provides the information necessary for a volitional response; the individual's positive volition is the spontaneous act by which salvation adjustment is made. God knew that response billions of years before it occurred and decreed it accordingly.

section: C. Foreknowledge of God in the Decrees
text: C. Foreknowledge of God in the Decrees

section: C. Foreknowledge of God in the Decrees
text: God foreknows all events as certainly future because He has first decreed them. Omniscience knows what is certainly future and also knows all the alternatives. Only reality is inserted into the decrees. Foreknowledge comes after the decrees and deals only with that reality. God's decrees relate equally to all future events of every kind, to the free actions of moral agents and to the actions of secondary causes alike.

section: C. Foreknowledge of God in the Decrees
text: Since the divine decrees alone establish certainty, nothing could be foreknown until it was first decreed. To place foreknowledge before the decrees would imply that God is responding to what another has caused — which is blasphemy. The members of the Trinity who foreknow, predestinate, and elect are the same persons of the Godhead, and no one is above or prior to them.

section: D. The Desires of God and the Decrees
text: D. The Desires of God and the Decrees

section: D. The Desires of God and the Decrees
text: The desires of God are aspects of the divine mind viewed separately, while the decrees of God are conceived as a whole. God is said to have no pleasure in the death of the wicked, yet the unbeliever's consignment to eternal judgment is part of His eternal purpose. Sin and death are displeasing to God; nevertheless they belong to His eternal decree, because God could only decree what He omnisciently knew the free will of each creature would produce. The will of God represents the ideal; the decrees represent the reality.

section: E. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: E. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees

section: E. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: A. All-comprehensive. Not the slightest uncertainty can exist regarding any event without introducing confusion into all events. Every decision, every act of volition, every consequence of every cause throughout all of history was known to God in eternity past. All events are interwoven and interdependent within one comprehensive system.

section: E. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: B. Eternal. God does not gain in knowledge. Whatever decisions are made in any given day, God knew them before time began. There never was a time when God did not know. We gain in knowledge; God does not. The decrees are not updated.

section: E. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: C. Perfect. God can only produce what is perfect. Like God Himself, His plans and works are perfect. The accuracy, the interwoven complexity, and the comprehensive cognizance of the decrees are all perfect.

section: E. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: D. Unchangeable and certain. Nothing can arise to necessitate change. Everything was decreed, known, and anticipated in eternity past.

section: E. Characteristics of the Divine Decrees
text: E. Free choice of divine sovereignty. God is not bound to follow a necessary course. Having decreed, however, God is bound by His infinite faithfulness, His veracity, and His truth to complete what He has begun. This is the doctrinal foundation of the third hope — the confident assurance that what God has begun for the mature believer, He will complete at the judgment seat of Christ.

section: F. The Extent of the Divine Decrees
text: F. The Extent of the Divine Decrees

section: F. The Extent of the Divine Decrees
text: God has decreed ends as well as means, causes as well as effects, conditions and instrumentalities as well as the events that depend upon them. Some things God has decreed to accomplish directly through immediate divine action — creation is the primary instance. Other things God brings to pass through secondary causes acting under the law of necessity. Other things God decrees to permit free agents to do through the exercise of their own volition. In every case, the decree renders the event certainly future, regardless of the category of causation.

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: The decrees unite in one all-inclusive and final objective: the satisfaction, manifestation, and glory of God. God's glory is what He is and what He thinks. Being the infinite One, the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are uniquely worthy of glory. As the subject of the divine decrees, it is inevitable that God will be glorified in what He has decreed, since the manifestation of His declarative glory also secures the highest good for His creatures — namely, cracking the maturity barrier and receiving the imputed blessings of time, parlayed into the imputed blessings of eternity.

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: The decrees are those sovereign purposes of God which are efficacious, accomplished by God alone, apart from all creature ability, mentality, talent, counsel, or cooperation. Salvation, preservation, logistical grace, and the programming of the ages all glorify God. When the believer cracks the maturity barrier and receives the imputed blessings of time, God is pleased and God is glorified.

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: The following summary points synthesize the doctrine of divine decrees as it bears on the believer's advance through the plan of God:

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: 1. The divine decrees are executed through imputation from the justice of God. There are seven imputations, all of which add up to the glory of God in the formula X + Y + Z.

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: 2. The decree of God allows maximum blessing for any believer, but recognizes that human volition can fall short of that potential. Only the reality of how far a believer advances is in the decrees; the potential is in omniscience.

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: 3. A positive response to doctrine can fulfill the maximum blessing God desires for the believer. To the extent every believer advances is the extent to which the decree of eternity past was recorded for that individual.

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: 4. God has the good sense to know beforehand how far each believer will travel, and that advance — and only that advance — was what was decreed.

section: G. The Divine Decrees and the Glory of God
text: 5. In too many cases the potential exceeds the reality. Only reality was decreed in eternity past. Nothing can be foreknown until it was first decreed. Omniscience knows all potentialities plus all realities; foreknowledge knows only the realities — the things which are decreed.

section: IV. Step Two — Reality in the Plan of God: Predestination (Romans 8:29b)
text: IV. Step Two — Reality in the Plan of God: Predestination (Romans 8:29b)

section: A. The Adjunctive Conjunction
text: A. The Adjunctive Conjunction

section: A. The Adjunctive Conjunction
text: The next phrase is introduced by the adjunctive use of the conjunction kai (καί), correctly translated also. Step two is added to step one: He also fore-ordained.

section: B. Prooorizō — The Verb of Predestination
text: B. Prooorizō — The Verb of Predestination

section: B. Prooorizō — The Verb of Predestination
text: The verb is the aorist active indicative of proorizō (προορίζω). The compound is pro (before) + horizō (ὁρίζω, to determine, to set a boundary, to decide). The meaning: to decide upon something beforehand, to predestinate someone as something, to pre-design, to fore-ordain. All of these renderings are interrelated and synonymous. This verb refers to the decrees or the plan of God in eternity past, specifically as they pertain to the church-age believer and the royal family of God.

section: B. Prooorizō — The Verb of Predestination
text: The aorist is a culminative aorist, viewing the decrees of God for the church-age believer in their entirety but regarding the result from the viewpoint of what exists — i.e., the last three steps of the five steps to glory. The active voice indicates God the Father, as author of the divine plan, producing the action in eternity past. The decrees were brought into simultaneous existence in eternity past. The indicative mood is the declarative indicative, asserting the reality of the divine decrees and the church-age believer's relationship to them.

section: B. Prooorizō — The Verb of Predestination
text: Corrected translation to this point: We know that whom He foreknew, He also fore-ordained.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step Two
text: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step Two

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step Two
text: Step two states that reality is in the plan of God — the decrees. Step one placed reality in the mind of God (foreknowledge). Step two places reality in the plan of God (the decrees). Every believer was in God's thoughts in eternity past, and every believer was also in God's plan — not merely anticipated but specifically and individually decreed.

section: C. The Doctrinal Content of Step Two
text: The purpose of the divine plan for each believer is to crack the maturity barrier in time, thereby parlaying the imputed blessings of time into the imputed blessings of eternity. God's decrees outline the most fabulous prosperity for the mature believer. The two judicial imputations of the Y radical — (1) all personal sins imputed to Christ and judged, and (2) divine righteousness imputed to the believer at salvation — constitute the basis for the real imputation of divine blessing in time, which is then parlayed into greater blessing in eternity.

section: D. Summorphous — Conformed Ones
text: D. Summorphous — Conformed Ones

section: D. Summorphous — Conformed Ones
text: The accusative masculine plural adjective summorphous (συμμόρφους) modifies the implied direct object. The word means conformed ones. He also predestinated us — conformed ones. The question of what the believer is conformed to is answered by the following phrase: to the image of His Son, which will be examined in the following chapter.

section: D. Summorphous — Conformed Ones
text: The term conformed ones refers to the royal family of God. This is a reference to the formation of the royal family at salvation through the baptism of the Holy Spirit, and therefore to current positional truth. It also carries the objective of phase two — maturity adjustment to the justice of God. Additionally, it takes cognizance of the third hope: the reality of blessing and reward in eternity at the judgment seat of Christ, including the resurrection body and the real imputation of eternal blessing.

section: D. Summorphous — Conformed Ones
text: The conformation in view moves through the entire formula. In the X radical, human life and Adam's original sin establish the first potential and the first hope, resolved by salvation adjustment. In the Y radical, the two judicial imputations establish the second potential and the second hope, with the point of conformation beginning at the cracking of the maturity barrier. In the Z radical, the imputation of eternal life plus the blessings of time at maturity establish the third potential, the third hope, and ultimately the seventh imputation at the judgment seat of Christ — the glory of God.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 1. Foreknowledge and omniscience are distinct operations of the divine intellect. Omniscience knows both the reality of every event and every alternative to that reality. Foreknowledge deals only with the reality — what actually occurs. The two are separated by the divine decrees: omniscience precedes the decrees; foreknowledge follows them.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 2. The chronological order is: omniscience → divine decrees → foreknowledge. This sequence, established in Acts 2:23, is not the emphasis of Romans 8:29, which presents foreknowledge, election, and predestination as coincidental with respect to their objects — the royal family of God. No chronological priority among these three is asserted in this passage.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 3. Nothing can be foreknown until it is first decreed. Only the divine decrees establish certainty. To place foreknowledge before the decrees implies that another has caused what occurs and that God is merely a passive observer — an inference that is theologically untenable.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 4. The decrees contain only reality, never the alternatives. All counterfactual and alternative history — what would have happened under different choices — resides within the omniscience of God alone. The decrees record what actually occurs, and foreknowledge acknowledges precisely what the decrees contain.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 5. Every believer was individually in the mind and plan of God before time began. This is the personal comfort of step one (foreknowledge) and step two (predestination): God knew each believer by name, knew the full extent of his advance in the plan of God, and decreed accordingly, billions of years before that believer existed.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 6. The will of God and the content of the decrees are distinct. God desires the maximum advance for every believer through the full X + Y + Z formula to the seventh imputation. The decrees contain only the reality of how far each believer actually advances. Where the potential exceeds the reality, the potential remains in omniscience; only the reality was decreed.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 7. The divine decrees are all-comprehensive, eternal, perfect, unchangeable, and free. Every event of every kind throughout all of history was known to God and decreed simultaneously in eternity past. The decrees do not develop by stages; they are one indivisible system of things, every link related to the essential integrity of the whole.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 8. The final objective of the divine decrees is the glory of God. The decrees unite in one all-inclusive purpose: the satisfaction, manifestation, and glory of God. This glory is realized in the believer's life through the seven imputations — culminating in the real imputation of eternal blessing and reward to the resurrection body at the judgment seat of Christ, which is the good of Romans 8:28.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 9. Proginōskō (to foreknow) is used in the New Testament exclusively with God as subject. The aorist tense is constative, gathering the totality of divine foreknowledge into one act. The active voice indicates God the Father as the author of the divine plan.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Seven
text: 10. Proorizō (to predestinate, to fore-ordain) refers specifically to the divine decrees for the church-age believer. The culminative aorist views those decrees in their entirety from the viewpoint of their existing results — the last three of the five steps to glory. The term summorphous (conformed ones) designates the royal family of God as the objects of this predestination.

section: Romans 8:29–30 — Divine Thinking, Predestination, and the Five Steps to Glory
text: Romans 8:29–30 — Divine Thinking, Predestination, and the Five Steps to Glory

section: Romans 8:29–30 — Divine Thinking, Predestination, and the Five Steps to Glory
text: Romans 8:28–30 “And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose. For those whom he foreknew he also predestined to be conformed to the image of his Son, in order that he might be the firstborn among many brothers. And those whom he predestined he also called, and those whom he called he also justified, and those whom he justified he also glorified.” (ESV)

section: Romans 8:29–30 — Divine Thinking, Predestination, and the Five Steps to Glory
text: Corrected translation: We know, in fact, that to those who love God — mature believers — all things work together for the purpose of good, to those who are the called according to a predetermined plan. Because whom He foreknew, He also foreordained — predestinated — conformed ones to the image of His Son, that He might be the firstborn among many brethren. And these same ones whom He foreordained, He also called.

section: Romans 8:29–30 — Divine Thinking, Predestination, and the Five Steps to Glory
text: Romans 8:28–30 presents the first two of five steps to glory — the mechanics by which all things work together for the purpose of the good. Verse 28 established the formula X + Y + Z = the glory of God through seven imputations spanning from physical birth to the resurrection body. Verse 29 introduces step one (divine thinking: omniscience, decrees, and foreknowledge) and step two (the divine purpose: predestination and conformity to the image of the Son). Verse 30 opens step three: entrance into the plan of God through election and calling. This chapter completes the exegesis of verse 29 and begins verse 30.

section: I. The Formula Reviewed: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God
text: I. The Formula Reviewed: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God

section: I. The Formula Reviewed: X + Y + Z = The Glory of God
text: The good of Romans 8:28 is the seventh and final imputation in God's plan for the Church Age believer — eternal blessings and rewards imputed to the resurrection body at the judgment seat of Christ. This good is the product of three radicals, each containing two imputations and a hope.

section: The X Radical: Birth and the First Potential
text: The X Radical: Birth and the First Potential

section: The X Radical: Birth and the First Potential
text: Imputation 1: Human life is imputed to the soul at physical birth — the beginning of individual existence. Imputation 2: Adam's original sin is simultaneously imputed to the old sin nature, producing spiritual death and establishing the first potential: salvation. Because all members of the human race are condemned at birth, salvation becomes the universal first potential. When an individual at the point of God consciousness is positive toward God, pertinent doctrine — the gospel — is provided. No geographical isolation and no linguistic barrier can prevent this provision for the person who is positive at God consciousness (Romans 1). The first potential plus the gospel equals the first hope: confident assurance of salvation.

text: The Y Radical: Judicial Imputations and the Second Potential

section: The Y Radical: Judicial Imputations and the Second Potential
text: The first hope is replaced by reality at the moment of faith in Christ — salvation adjustment to the justice of God. The Y radical then opens a new horizon. Judicial imputation 3: all personal sins of the world are imputed to Christ on the cross and judged. There is no antecedence — these sins were alien to the impeccable humanity of Christ. text: divine righteousness (+R) is imputed to the believer at salvation — again with no antecedence, no merit, no equivalence on the human side. This +R becomes the target and home — the system of antecedence — for blessing in time. The second potential is the potential of great blessing in time. When positive volition toward doctrine is sustained, the second hope forms: confident assurance that consistent doctrine intake will produce spiritual maturity and the real imputation of blessing in time.

text: The Z Radical: Eternal Life and the Third Potential

section: The Z Radical: Eternal Life and the Third Potential
text: Imputation 5: eternal life is imputed to the regenerate human spirit at salvation. Imputation 6: blessing in time is imputed to the believer's

section: The Z Radical: Eternal Life and the Third Potential
text: Imputation 6: blessing in time is imputed to the believer's +R at the point of maturity adjustment to the justice of God. The second hope is replaced by the reality of maturity; a third hope must therefore be established. The third potential is blessing and reward in eternity. This potential, combined with pertinent doctrine and undeserved suffering, produces the third hope: confident assurance of great blessing and reward at the judgment seat of Christ. This is the hope operative at dying grace, expressed by Paul in 2 Timothy 4:7–8: "I have fought the good fight, I have finished the course, I have kept the faith; henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness."

section: The Seventh Imputation: The Good
text: The Seventh Imputation: The Good

section: The Seventh Imputation: The Good
text: Imputation 7: eternal blessings and rewards are imputed to the resurrection body at the judgment seat of Christ. This is a real imputation and therefore has two factors: factor one is the content — the blessings and rewards themselves, which glorify the Lord forever; factor two is the home — the resurrection body, minus the old sin nature, as the system of antecedence and affinity. There is a perfect correspondence between the blessings imputed and the resurrection body that receives them.

section: The Seventh Imputation: The Good
text: The seven imputations in sequence: (1) human life imputed to the soul at birth; (2) Adam's original sin imputed to the old sin nature at birth; (3) all personal sins imputed to Christ on the cross; (4) divine righteousness imputed to the believer at salvation; (5) eternal life imputed to the regenerate human spirit at salvation; (6) blessing in time imputed to

section: The Seventh Imputation: The Good
text: (6) blessing in time imputed to +R at maturity; (7) eternal blessings and rewards imputed to the resurrection body at the judgment seat of Christ.

section: Grammatical Analysis: 'To the Image of His Son'
text: Grammatical Analysis: 'To the Image of His Son'

section: Grammatical Analysis: 'To the Image of His Son'
text: The phrase rendered "to the image of his Son" involves a descriptive genitive singular from the noun eikōn (εἰκών), correctly translated image — a likeness or representation. With this descriptive genitive is a possessive genitive from huios (υἱός), referring to the Lord Jesus Christ, together with a possessive genitive from the intensive pronoun used as a personal pronoun: autos (αὐτός). In Greek, there is no third person personal pronoun. The first person is egō (ἐγώ); the second is su (σύ). For the third person, autos serves as both intensive pronoun and personal pronoun, supplying the referent "His" in the phrase "the image of His Son."

section: Theological Content: Conformed Ones
text: Theological Content: Conformed Ones

section: Theological Content: Conformed Ones
text: "Conformed ones" refers positionally to every Church Age believer, who is placed in union with Christ at salvation through the baptism of the Holy Spirit. Retroactive positional truth divorces the believer from the old sin nature — the former master — and current positional truth establishes the foundational reality of conformity to the image of the Son. This is the positional dimension.

section: Theological Content: Conformed Ones
text: The experiential dimension operates between salvation and the resurrection. Between union with Christ at salvation and the reception of the resurrection body in eternity, there is only one pathway of conformity: the daily function of the Grace Apparatus for Perception (GAP), producing maturity adjustment to the justice of God. No system of works, no ascetic discipline, no financial giving, no ordinance observance, no service organization, no form of human good can produce experiential conformity. Doctrine taken into the soul is the exclusive mechanism.

section: Theological Content: Conformed Ones
text: The ultimate dimension is the resurrection body itself — the conformity is completed at the rapture, when every Church Age believer receives a resurrection body exactly like that of the Son of God, minus the old sin nature, minus human good. Even the believer who was maximally negative toward doctrine in time receives this resurrection body, because it is given unconditionally at the rapture. It becomes, however, the basis for building: blessing in time — obtained only through GAP — is parlayed into the seventh imputation, eternal blessing and reward. The believer who was entirely negative toward doctrine has the resurrection body and nothing more. There will be no tears in eternity, but there will be great variation in the blessings and rewards imputed to the resurrection body.

section: The Three Stages of Sanctification
text: The Three Stages of Sanctification

section: The Three Stages of Sanctification
text: The phrase "conformed ones to the image of His Son" recapitulates the three stages of sanctification. Stage one is positional sanctification: union with Christ through the baptism of the Holy Spirit at salvation. Stage two is experiential sanctification: advancing toward maturity through the daily function of GAP. Stage three is ultimate sanctification: the resurrection body, received at the rapture. This is the Father's plan for the royal family of God.

section: "That He Might Be the Firstborn" — Grammatical and Theological Analysis
text: "That He Might Be the Firstborn" — Grammatical and Theological Analysis

section: "That He Might Be the Firstborn" — Grammatical and Theological Analysis
text: The purpose clause "that He might be" is expressed in Greek as a prepositional idiom: eis (εἰς) plus the accusative of the definite article, plus the present active infinitive of the verb eimi (εἶναι). The static present indicates a condition that perpetually exists. The active voice designates the Lord Jesus Christ — in resurrection body, in ascension and session — as the one producing the action. The infinitive of purpose is correctly translated "that He might be."

section: "That He Might Be the Firstborn" — Grammatical and Theological Analysis
text: The referent "He" is derived not from the article but from the accusative singular of general reference from the intensive pronoun autos (αὐτός), which in the accusative functions as the logical subject of the infinitive — describing the one connected with the action and properly translated as the third person singular pronoun.

section: "That He Might Be the Firstborn" — Grammatical and Theological Analysis
text: The object of the infinitive is the accusative singular direct object from prōtotokos (πρωτότοκος), correctly translated firstborn. Full corrected translation: "that He might be the firstborn." Colossians 1:15 provides the parallel: "who keeps on being the exact image of the unseen God, the privileged firstborn with reference to all creatures."

section: Three Connotations of Firstborn
text: Three Connotations of Firstborn

section: Three Connotations of Firstborn
text: First, firstborn connotes rulership. Christ is the firstborn, which means He is the ruler — at present, of the Church, the royal family of God, and at the Second Advent, of the world.

section: Three Connotations of Firstborn
text: Second, the firstborn is the family priest. Christ is ordained a royal priest forever after the order of Melchizedek (Hebrews 5–7).

section: Three Connotations of Firstborn
text: Third, the firstborn possesses the double portion. Christ has two kingdoms of believers: Israel, over whom He rules as Son of David, and the Church, over whom He rules as King of Kings. The emphasis in Romans 8:29 is on His rulership of the royal family of God.

section: "Among Many Brethren" — The Royal Family
text: "Among Many Brethren" — The Royal Family

section: "Among Many Brethren" — The Royal Family
text: The phrase "among many brethren" involves en (ἐν) plus the dative plural of polus (πολύς) plus the noun adelphos (ἀδελφός). The "many brethren" are Church Age believers — the royal family of God. Corrected translation of the full verse: "We know that whom He foreknew, He also foreordained — predestinated — conformed ones to the image of His Son, that He might be the firstborn among many brethren, the royal family of God, or Church Age believer."

section: "Among Many Brethren" — The Royal Family
text: The royal family of God was formed in eternity past. Christ is the firstborn of the royal family — its ruler, its high priest, and the holder of the double portion heritage. The many brethren — Church Age believers — constitute that royal family. All of this is designed to read the believer into the big picture: to understand how the divine decrees relate to the seven imputations, and to bring the believer to the objective in time — maturity adjustment to the justice of God.

section: III. Step Three: Entrance into the Plan of God — Election and Calling (Romans 8:30a)
text: III. Step Three: Entrance into the Plan of God — Election and Calling (Romans 8:30a)

section: Connective Particle and Demonstrative Pronoun
text: Connective Particle and Demonstrative Pronoun

section: Connective Particle and Demonstrative Pronoun
text: Verse 30 opens with the post-positive conjunctive particle de (δέ) in a connective use, correctly translated and — linking verse 30 to verse 29 as a continuation of the same sequence of steps, rather than a contrast.

section: Connective Particle and Demonstrative Pronoun
text: The subject is the accusative masculine plural from the relative pronoun hos (ὅς), "whom," followed by the aorist active indicative of proorizō (προορίζω) carried over from verse 29 — "whom He foreordained." The object "these same ones" is the accusative plural demonstrative pronoun houtos (οὗτος), the immediate demonstrative referring to what has immediately preceded. It cannot be translated merely as "them" — its force is these same ones, emphasizing continuity with the Church Age believers already in view.

section: The Verb Kaleō: Technical Sense — Election
text: The Verb Kaleō: Technical Sense — Election

section: The Verb Kaleō: Technical Sense — Election
text: The verb is the aorist active indicative of kaleō (καλέω), meaning to call, to name, to designate, to summon, to invite. Here it is used in the technical theological sense for the doctrine of election. The culminative aorist regards the doctrine of election for the royal family of God in its entirety, viewing it from the standpoint of existing results. The active voice designates God the Father as the author of the divine decrees and the divine plan. The declarative indicative mood states a dogmatic reality: all Church Age believers are elected. Every believer is in the plan of God.

section: Election Defined in Relation to the X Radical
text: Election Defined in Relation to the X Radical

section: Election Defined in Relation to the X Radical
text: Election is the point of the decision — specifically, the moment of faith in Jesus Christ. In the X radical: human life plus Adam's original sin equals the first potential; that potential plus the gospel equals the first hope; the first hope converted through faith in Christ is the point of election. Election emphasizes the fact that the believer is permanently in the plan of God. Second Timothy 1:9 states: "the One having saved us and having elected the royal family into a holy station of life, not according to our works, but according to His predetermined plan — even grace which has been given to us in Christ Jesus before human history, before the times of the dispensations."

section: The Relationship of Election, Foreknowledge, and Predestination
text: The Relationship of Election, Foreknowledge, and Predestination

section: The Relationship of Election, Foreknowledge, and Predestination
text: These three are simultaneous functions within the divine decrees, each with a distinct emphasis. Election is the point of the decision: the moment a given individual believes in Christ. Foreknowledge is the recognition of that decision: God's prior cognizance of the reality of what the individual's free will would do. Predestination is the function of the decisions: God's prior knowledge of what the believer will do at each subsequent point in time — the reality of all future decisions. All three face reality exclusively; none deal with alternatives. Omniscience encompasses both the reality and all alternatives. The decrees contain only reality. Foreknowledge, election, and predestination acknowledge only what is in the decrees.

section: The Relationship of Election, Foreknowledge, and Predestination
text: Predestination does not coerce the free will. It is prior knowledge of what the free will will freely choose. The sum total of the decisions a person makes across a lifetime — every wise and every foolish decision, every advance and every retreat in the spiritual life — constitutes the reality placed in the decrees. What omniscience knows as alternatives (what would have happened had a different decision been made) is never in the decrees and is never the object of foreknowledge or predestination.

section: The Relationship of Election, Foreknowledge, and Predestination
text: The order of logical sequence (as per Acts 2:23) is: first omniscience — which knows everything, including all alternatives; then the decrees — which contain only reality; then foreknowledge — which recognizes only what is in the decrees. The decrees of God for the Church Age cover the entirety of the royal family from Pentecost to the rapture: every person, every decision, every consequence.

section: Security and the Plan of God
text: Security and the Plan of God

section: Security and the Plan of God
text: There is no greater security than the recognition that before human history began, the believer's entrance into the plan of God was known in the omniscience of God, inserted into the decrees as reality, and guaranteed. The blessings of maturity adjustment were provided for the mature believer even before Adam existed. The decrees contain the most extraordinary and unique blessings for mature believers — blessings far exceeding anything available in the garden of Eden.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: The formula X + Y + Z = the glory of God is the target of a comprehensive and systematic assault. At every node of the plan, a specific attack is mounted.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against imputation 1 (human life at birth): the theory of evolution, which denies the direct creation of human life and the reality of individual existence as God's act.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against imputation 2 (Adam's original sin): the assault on the dignity of man through denial of the fall and its consequences — spiritual death and condemnation at birth.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against the first potential (salvation): the full range of philosophical systems that offer alternative explanations for human existence and destiny, foreclosing the gospel before it can be heard.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against the first hope and the point of election (faith in Christ): the corruption of the gospel through addition or subtraction — faith plus baptism, faith plus church membership, faith plus emotional response, faith plus works of any kind.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against judicial imputation 1 (sins imputed to Christ): the substitution of a physical theory of atonement — that Christ's physical blood, rather than the spiritual work of bearing the penalty of sin, is the basis of redemption.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against judicial imputation 2 (divine righteousness imputed at salvation): widespread ignorance of this doctrine produces a failure to understand the basis for blessing in time.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against the second potential (blessing in time): the attack of false austerity — the teaching that material prosperity is evidence of worldliness, that God blesses only those who divest themselves of all earthly goods, and that Christian credibility requires visible poverty.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against the second hope and the maturity plus (maturity adjustment): the substitution of activity for doctrine — witnessing, prayer, church service, missionary work, discipleship programs, and Christian service organizations are presented as the path to spiritual maturity, displacing the daily function of GAP.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against the Z radical and eternal security: the denial of the permanent nature of salvation, requiring repeated acts of repentance and faith after every failure.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against blessing in time: the equation of prosperity with worldliness — so that the very blessings God designs for the mature believer become a source of guilt and accusation.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against the third potential (blessing and reward in eternity): the claim that eternal rewards are tied exclusively to evangelistic activity or visible Christian service, bypassing the doctrine of the judgment seat of Christ and the seven imputations.

section: IV. Satan's Attack on the Seven Imputations
text: Against undeserved suffering: the inability to interpret it theologically, so that what God designs to maintain the third hope instead produces confusion, bitterness, or retreat. The result in every case is to redirect the believer from X + Y + Z = glory toward the devil's triangle: the old sin nature as the ruler of life, expressed through personal sin, human good, and evil.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 1. The seven imputations span the entirety of the believer's existence. From physical birth (human life and Adam's original sin) through salvation (judicial imputations 3 and 4, plus eternal life) through maturity (blessing in time) to eternity (blessing and reward at the judgment seat of Christ) — the plan of God is a seamless, integrated sequence with affinity between what is imputed and the recipient at each stage.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 2. The good of Romans 8:28 is the seventh imputation. It is a real imputation with two factors: factor one is the content — eternal blessings and rewards that glorify the Lord forever; factor two is the home — the resurrection body, minus the old sin nature, as the system of antecedence.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 3. Being conformed to the image of the Son operates in three dimensions. Positionally, all Church Age believers are conformed ones now through union with Christ via the baptism of the Holy Spirit. Experientially, conformity advances between salvation and eternity only through the daily function of GAP leading to maturity adjustment. Ultimately, every Church Age believer will be conformed at the rapture through the reception of a resurrection body like that of the Son of God.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 4. The worst believer who ever lived receives a resurrection body at the rapture. This is unconditional and guaranteed. It constitutes the basis for building — but without blessing in time through GAP, there is nothing above and beyond the resurrection body itself. The believer with zero doctrine has a resurrection body and nothing more at the judgment seat of Christ. There are no tears in eternity, but there is no equality either.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 5. Election is the doctrine that relates the believer to the plan of God from eternity past. Election coincides with foreknowledge and predestination. Election emphasizes the fact of being permanently in the plan of God; foreknowledge is God's prior recognition of the decision of faith; predestination is God's prior knowledge of all subsequent decisions. All three deal exclusively with reality — what actually occurs — not with alternatives. Omniscience alone encompasses the alternatives.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 6. The order of divine thinking is: omniscience → decrees → foreknowledge. Nothing can be foreknown until it is first decreed. The decrees establish reality. Omniscience is the broader term, encompassing everything that could happen and all alternatives. The decrees contain only what actually happens. Foreknowledge acknowledges only what is in the decrees. This sequence, established in Acts 2:23, is the foundation for understanding the plan of God.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 7. Predestination does not coerce free will. It is prior knowledge of what the free will will freely do. The sum of a believer's actual decisions across a lifetime constitutes the reality placed in the decrees. The alternatives — what would have happened had different decisions been made — belong to omniscience, not to the decrees or foreknowledge.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 8. There is no greater security than the eternal guarantee embedded in the divine decrees. Before human history began, the omniscience of God knew who would believe in Christ, inserted that reality into the decrees, and guaranteed the blessings of maturity adjustment. Those blessings were provided for the mature believer before Adam existed — blessings exceeding anything available in the garden of Eden.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 9. Christ's designation as firstborn carries three connotations. Rulership — He is ruler of the Church now and of the world at the Second Advent. Priesthood — He is ordained a royal priest forever after the order of Melchizedek. Double portion — He rules both Israel as Son of David and the Church as King of Kings.

section: Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Twenty-Eight
text: 10. The only path of experiential conformity between salvation and eternity is GAP. Works, perfect conduct, charitable giving, ordinance observance, emotional experience, ascetic discipline — none of these produce experiential conformity to the image of the Son. Bible doctrine taken into the soul and metabolized through the Grace Apparatus for Perception is the exclusive mechanism. Without it, there is no maturity adjustment, no second hope, no blessing in time, and therefore no seventh imputation above the baseline of the resurrection body.
